Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Paul Schaaf <sch...@u.washington.edu> writes:

>If someone uses a Hidden Lurker to deny Joe Shmoe (who has recruited a
>Wolf Companion or other retainer with a strike) his strike, can the
>retainer still strike? It kind of surprised me when this came up in a
>game and I hadn't seen it before. I love it when that happens!

Since the retainer's damage is not a strike, yes - the retainer still
does damage (assuming the round is at close range in the case of the
Wolf Companion, of course.

Messages.Author: Jon Ferro
Messages.Body:
Paul Schaaf <sch...@u.washington.edu> writes:
If someone uses a Hidden Lurker to deny Joe Shmoe (who has recruited a
Wolf Companion or other retainer with a strike) his strike, can the
retainer still strike? It kind of surprised me when this came up in a
game and I hadn't seen it before. I love it when that happens!

The question is simply answered by paying attention to your terminology.
Wolf Companion, Murder of Crows, et al, do NOT HAVE STRIKES; they simply
do extra damage during combat. Therefore, that damage is done
regardless of whether the controlling minion is allowed to strike.

P.S. We also play with a house rule that the Wolf Companion damage only
occurs at close range. Comments?

Messages.Author: Bob Ellison
Messages.Body:
> If someone uses a Hidden Lurker to deny Joe Shmoe (who has recruited a
> Wolf Companion or other retainer with a strike) his strike, can the
> retainer still strike? It kind of surprised me when this came up in a
> game and I hadn't seen it before. I love it when that happens!

Wolf Companion and Murder of Crows do not have strikes. They simply
do damage. This damage cannot be dodged (as you can only dodge strikes).
It can be prevented, though, with normal damage prevention cards.

So, yes, the Wolf Companion or the Murder of Crows do damage to
Hidden Lurkers.

I'm not sure about the Ghoul Retainer; but I believe his damage is done
by strike, and as such cannot be used against a Hidden Lurker on the
first round.

papillo the phonetic

: cr...@Ra.MsState.Edu (Charles Richard Robb) writes:

: >Wolf COmpanion ONLY does its damage at close range. It has been ruled that the

: So what's the explanation for making Wolf Companion short range?
: Nothing in the card text, for 'reality', or in the interest of game
: balance suggests that it should be.

ALL strikes only take effect at close range, UNLESS the card specifically
says so otherwise (in words, or by putting R after the damage.)

Besides that, there has been a specific ruling that Aid from Crows and
Wolf Companion are identical in all respects, EXCEPT that Aid from Crows
can be used at long range and Wolf Companion may only be used at close.
Look it up in the DTRs if you don[t believe me, or see L. Scott Johnson's
Card Rulings file (posted to this group less than a week ago) which
re-quotes the DTR in its entirety.

Messages.Author: Aaron Mandelbaum
Messages.Body:
In article <3l5c4h$b...@tribune.usask.ca> sht...@duke.usask.ca (Shane Hamish William Travis) writes:

>: So what's the explanation for making Wolf Companion short range?
>: Nothing in the card text, for 'reality', or in the interest of game
>: balance suggests that it should be.

>ALL strikes only take effect at close range, UNLESS the card specifically
>says so otherwise (in words, or by putting R after the damage.)

But it's not a strike. It's damage done during damage resolution. As it's
worded, dodge, for example, would do nothing against it.

>Besides that, there has been a specific ruling that Aid from Crows and
>Wolf Companion are identical in all respects, EXCEPT that Aid from Crows
>can be used at long range and Wolf Companion may only be used at close.

Okay, then, there's a good reason: there's another card identical, which
says it can be used at long range (I assume it *does* say that, I've never
actually seen one). Which means that they should have had 'if at close
range' on the card, but that's just errata.

If you'd said "It was supposed to say 'only useable at close range' on the
card, but they left it off", then I would have believed you. Instead, you
(or whoever) said the *interpretation* was 'only at close range', which
makes no sense.
